Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our legal team's proposed redlines to the Order Form and MSA. Two items are blocking sign:

We included a marked PDF (CloudNova-Proposed-Redlines-0504.pdf) with language. Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood can accept a structured carve-out with a monetary ceiling tied to the annual contract value rather than unlimited exposure?

- Redwood's standard position: we accept an IP indemnity (we indemnify against third-party IP claims for our models/software when there's a valid claim), and we already carve IP indemnity out from the general liability cap in our template MSA.
- The sticking point is scope and the monetary exposure. We typically accept an "IP indemnity carve-out" but prefer to limit remediation/royalty obligations to a defined multiple of the order value (e.g., 2x-3x ACV) or a fixed cap tied to escrow/insurance, not an unlimited liability.
- The notice/remediation timeline you proposed is reasonable operationally; we want to preserve cure/triage time and allow for investigation with vendors.

Karthik / Rishi / Monica — can you review the attached CloudNova PDF and propose counter-language that: (a) preserves an IP carve-out for indemnity, (b) sets a capped monetary exposure (suggest 3x ACV or a $XM floor), and (c) keeps the 14/90 timeline but adds an initial triage period and the ability to extend by mutual agreement for complex claims?

I'll offer to CloudNova that we can accept a structured cap coupled with evidence-based remediation steps and an insurance-first recovery path.

Thanks,

Thanks — drafted suggested language below (attached as MillerKent-Redlines-0507.docx for track changes). Key points:

- IP indemnity carve-out: Redwood agrees to indemnify and defend Customer for third-party IP infringement claims resulting directly from Redwood's Deliverables; liability for such claims shall be subject to a separate IP-remediation cap equal to the greater of (i) three times the annual contract value (ACV) under the Order Form, or (ii) $500,000.
- Insurance-first: Customer must tender the claim to its available insurance prior to Redwood's payment obligation; Redwood will cooperate with insurance carriers and has rights of subrogation.
- Notice & remediation timeline: Customer must provide prompt written notice within 30 days of discovery; Redwood will acknowledge receipt within 5 business days, provide an initial triage and proposed remediation approach within 14 calendar days, and use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve within 120 calendar days; the parties may agree to extensions for complex suits.
- Exclusivity and settlement control: Redwood may assume control of defense with consent for any settlement that imposes monetary obligations; if Redwood declines control, indemnity obligations remain but monetary exposure is capped by the IP-remediation cap above.

I recommend we offer the attached redline to CloudNova with a short negotiating FAQ that explains: why 3x ACV (predictable economics), the insurance-first approach, and the triage timeline to avoid frivolous claims.

Rishi
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
Attachment: MillerKent-Redlines-0507.docx (track changes; key clauses highlighted)
